venues.name: Federation Square
venues.note: Melbourne's angular civic heart, facing Flinders Street Station across the river, a good first anchor for orienting the city, with the Ian Potter Centre and ACMI opening off the plaza. A private guide can start you here and walk you into the laneways within minutes.

venues.name: Hosier Lane street art
venues.note: The most famous of Melbourne's graffiti bluestone lanes, a wall-to-wall canvas that changes weekly and runs off Flinders Lane opposite Fed Square. Even a short walk-through gives the family the city's counter-culture in ten minutes; nearby Rutledge Lane extends it.

venues.name: Degraves Street
venues.note: A narrow cobbled lane packed with awning-shaded cafe tables, the postcard of Melbourne's coffee culture. Order a flat white standing at a hole-in-the-wall roaster and watch the city's obsession up close.

venues.name: The Block Arcade & Royal Arcade
venues.note: Two exquisitely preserved Victorian-era shopping arcades: the Block with its mosaic-tiled floor and the historic Hopetoun Tea Rooms, and Royal Arcade with its Gog and Magog figures. Genteel, unhurried and a lovely stop between laneways for tea and chocolate.

venues.name: National Gallery of Victoria, International (NGV)
venues.note: Australia's oldest and most-visited public gallery, whose St Kilda Road building holds the international collection behind a famous water-wall entrance. The blockbuster summer exhibitions and the stained-glass Great Hall ceiling are worth timed tickets; entry to the permanent collection is free.

venues.name: NGV Australia, Ian Potter Centre
venues.note: The Fed Square site of the NGV devoted entirely to Australian art, including the country's most significant collection of Indigenous art. A shorter, focused visit that pairs naturally with Federation Square for a multi-generation morning.

venues.name: Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria
venues.note: Thirty-eight hectares of lakes, lawns and rare plantings sweeping down toward the river, Melbourne's green lungs and an easy, buggy-friendly wander for elders and children alike. Take the Aboriginal Heritage Walk or an Punt Road picnic; the Tan track circles it.

venues.name: Shrine of Remembrance
venues.note: Melbourne's grand war memorial on a rise above the Botanic Gardens, its ceremonial forecourt and city views making it one of the CBD's most dignified vantage points. Climb to the balcony for the sightline straight down Swanston Street to the city.

venues.name: Queen Victoria Market
venues.note: A sprawling 19th-century open-air market, delis, produce, seafood and the Winter/Summer Night Markets, and the best single place to graze the city's food cultures in one visit. A guided Ultimate Foodie tour lets the family taste widely without the crush.
credentials: Victorian Heritage Register, listed 19th-century market

venues.name: Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG)
venues.note: The spiritual home of Australian sport and one of the world's great stadiums, holding 100,000 for AFL and cricket. A behind-the-scenes tour of the members' rooms and the arena thrills any sports-loving traveller; a Boxing Day Test or an AFL final is a bucket-list day.

venues.name: National Sports Museum
venues.note: Inside the MCG, an immersive museum of Australian sport, cricket, AFL, the Olympics and the Australian Open, with interactive galleries the children will not want to leave. Combine it with the stadium tour.

venues.name: Melbourne Skydeck (Eureka Tower)
venues.note: The Southern Hemisphere's highest public viewing platform, on the 88th floor at 285m, with 360-degree views and 'The Edge' glass cube that slides out over the city. Best at dusk to catch daylight then the lit skyline; the recently rebranded Eureka Skydeck.

venues.name: State Library Victoria
venues.note: One of the world's most beautiful reading rooms, the domed octagonal La Trobe Reading Room, free to enter and quietly spectacular from the upper galleries. A serene pause from the CBD, and home to the Ned Kelly armour.

venues.name: Immigration Museum
venues.note: Housed in the old Customs House, it tells the story of the peoples who built Melbourne, a resonant stop for Indian families, tracing the migration threads that make the city so plural today.

venues.name: Royal Exhibition Building & Carlton Gardens
venues.note: Australia's first UNESCO-listed building, a soaring 1880 exhibition palace set in formal Victorian gardens beside Melbourne Museum. Time a dome-promenade tour; the gardens are a lovely picnic setting for elders and children.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Royal Exhibition Building and Carlton Gardens

venues.name: Melbourne Museum
venues.note: A modern natural-history and cultural museum beside the Exhibition Building, with the Bunjilaka Aboriginal Cultural Centre, a living rainforest gallery and the beloved racehorse Phar Lap. Genuinely absorbing across three generations, and there is an IMAX alongside.

venues.name: Fitzroy, Brunswick Street & Gertrude Street
venues.note: Melbourne's original bohemian quarter and still its most characterful, independent boutiques, record shops, wine bars and some of the city's best small dining. The neighbourhood to walk slowly with a coffee and let the family drift.

venues.name: Collingwood & Smith Street
venues.note: Once industrial, now the city's hottest strip, Smith Street runs from cult roasters to natural-wine bars and the rooftop of the old Foy & Gibson warehouses. A cool-hunter's afternoon for younger travellers.

venues.name: Brunswick, Sydney Road & Lygon Street north
venues.note: A multicultural strip of Middle Eastern grocers, live-music rooms and third-wave cafes, north of the centre and refreshingly un-touristed. Good for a driver to loop through for a taste of the real, everyday Melbourne.

venues.name: Lygon Street, Carlton, Little Italy
venues.note: The historic Italian quarter where Melbourne's espresso culture began, lined with trattorias and gelaterie. An easy, crowd-pleasing dinner street a short hop from the Exhibition Building and museum.

venues.name: St Kilda Pier & the little-penguin colony
venues.note: A newly rebuilt pier reaching into Port Phillip Bay, where around 1,400 wild little penguins come ashore at dusk on the breakwater, free to view from the boardwalk. A magical, gentle evening for children; go at sunset and keep torches off.

venues.name: Luna Park Melbourne
venues.note: The 1912 amusement park behind its famous grinning Mr Moon face on the Esplanade, home to one of the world's oldest continually operating roller-coasters (the Scenic Railway). Nostalgic and photogenic; open weekends and holidays.

venues.name: The Esplanade & St Kilda foreshore
venues.note: Melbourne's bayside promenade, palm-lined beach, Sunday art market, and the grand old Espy hotel, an easy seaside afternoon 15 minutes from the CBD. Cakes on Acland Street's continental-cake row are a ritual.

venues.name: Southbank & the Yarra promenade
venues.note: The riverside arts-and-dining precinct across from Flinders Street, Arts Centre spire, restaurants along the water, and the launch point for river cruises. A pleasant sundown stroll with the skyline reflected in the Yarra.

venues.name: Yarra River cruise
venues.note: A relaxed way to read the city from the water, sightseeing cruises run upriver toward the gardens and downriver to Docklands and the port. Charter a private vessel for a multi-gen group; a slow, low-effort highlight for elders.

venues.name: Docklands & The District
venues.note: A modern waterfront quarter of marinas, waterside dining and public art west of the CBD, reached by the free City Circle tram. Calmer than the centre and good for a harbourside lunch; the Melbourne Star wheel here is undergoing a planned reopening.

venues.name: Arts Centre Melbourne
venues.note: Under its lattice spire, the city's flagship performing-arts complex, ballet, opera, theatre and the Melbourne Symphony at Hamer Hall. Worth a night out; the Sunday market of makers runs along its forecourt.

venues.name: Abbotsford Convent
venues.note: A 19th-century convent turned rambling arts precinct on the riverbank, galleries, artist studios, gardens and the excellent Lentil As Anything and Convent Bakery. Free to wander, deeply atmospheric, and next to Collingwood Children's Farm for the little ones.

venues.name: Fitzroy Gardens & Cooks' Cottage
venues.note: A grand formal park on the CBD's edge, with elm avenues, a fairy tree and the transplanted stone cottage of Captain Cook's family, shipped brick-by-brick from England. A short, shaded green stop for elders between sights.

venues.name: Chinatown & Little Bourke Street
venues.note: One of the oldest continuous Chinatowns in the Western world, its arches spanning Little Bourke Street, with the Chinese Museum tucked among the restaurants. The address for late dumplings and the setting of Flower Drum.

venues.name: Flower Drum
venues.note: Melbourne's legendary Cantonese fine-diner, quietly running for over forty years on Market Lane, Peking duck, aromatic baked crab, and discreet, faultless service. The special-occasion dinner for a discerning family; book well ahead.
credentials: The Age Good Food Guide 2026, Two Hats
The Age Good Food Guide 2026, Restaurant of the Year

venues.name: Chin Chin
venues.note: The buzzing, all-day Southeast Asian diner on Flinders Lane that has drawn queues since 2011, hawker-style shared plates built for a table of many. Lively, generous and easy for a mixed group; the 'Feed Me' menu takes the decisions away.
credentials: A landmark modern Melbourne dining room, an enduring institution

venues.name: Vue de Monde
venues.note: Melbourne's landmark fine-dining room on the 55th floor of the Rialto, a native-ingredient degustation with the whole city at your feet. The city's dress-up dinner; request a window and let the sommelier lead.
credentials: The Age Good Food Guide 2026, Three Hats

venues.name: Attica
venues.note: Ben Shewry's celebrated suburban restaurant, long ranked among the world's best, serving a deeply personal tasting menu of native Australian ingredients. A pilgrimage table for serious food travellers; reservations open in advance and go fast.
credentials: The Age Good Food Guide 2026, Two Hats

venues.name: Flinders Lane dining
venues.note: The single best street to eat in Melbourne, a dense run of hatted restaurants and wine bars from Movida's tapas to Cumulus Inc. Let a concierge match the room to your group; walkable end to end.

venues.name: Melbourne coffee crawl
venues.note: Coffee is a genuine civic craft here, a private roaster-hopping morning through hole-in-the-wall bars and single-origin cafes reveals the culture better than any sight. Ask for a barista-led tasting; the flat white is the local benchmark.

venues.name: Yarra Valley wineries (day trip)
venues.note: An hour east, Victoria's premier cool-climate wine region, cellar doors from Domaine Chandon's French sparkling house to acclaimed Pinot and Chardonnay estates, with long lunches among the vines. Ideal as a chauffeured day; several estates cater beautifully to non-drinkers and families.

venues.name: Dandenong Ranges & Puffing Billy (day trip)
venues.note: An hour east into fern-gullied mountain forest, riding the century-old Puffing Billy steam train with legs dangling from open carriages, pure delight for children and grandparents alike. Add the William Ricketts sanctuary and a Sassafras tea room.

venues.name: Sovereign Hill, Ballarat (day trip)
venues.note: A vast, living re-creation of a 1850s gold-rush town about 90 minutes west, costumed streets, gold panning, and a nightly sound-and-light show. Immersive and hands-on for multi-generation groups curious about how Victoria's wealth was made.

venues.name: Werribee Park Mansion & Shadowfax (day trip)
venues.note: A grand 1870s Italianate mansion in formal gardens 30 minutes south-west, beside Shadowfax winery and the Werribee Open Range Zoo. A gentle, elegant half-day that combines heritage, wine and a safari-style drive for children.

venues.name: Melbourne's parks & gardens promenade
venues.note: The linked chain of parkland ringing the CBD, Kings Domain, Alexandra Gardens and the riverbank, makes for a long, level walk or a hired-bike loop past the Shrine and the rowing sheds. An easy way to see the city's famed green ring.

venues.name: Australian Open (seasonal, January)
venues.note: The year's first tennis Grand Slam, drawing the world to Melbourne Park each January, night sessions under lights at Rod Laver Arena are electric. Corporate suites and premium hospitality make it a marquee outing; book the season far ahead.

venues.name: Australian Grand Prix (seasonal, March)
venues.note: Formula 1 returns to the parkland circuit around Albert Park Lake each autumn, a fast street-style track minutes from the CBD. Trackside paddock and grandstand packages suit a group of enthusiasts; the city hums all weekend.

venues.name: Melbourne Cup Carnival (seasonal, November)
venues.note: 'The race that stops a nation', the first Tuesday of November at Flemington, the centrepiece of a spring carnival of fashion, marquees and champagne. The Birdcage enclosure is the ticket for a memorable, dressed-up day.

venues.name: Caretaker's Cottage
venues.note: A tiny 1850s bluestone gatehouse turned world-ranked bar, an English-pub soul, faultless drinks, and Guinness on draught.
